ACT.1.1-3.text: Jesus appears to the apostles for forty days

ACT.1.4-5.text: Jesus tells the apostles to wait in Jerusalem

ACT.1.21-23.text: The believers propose Joseph and Matthias as apostle

ACT.1.24-26.text: The believers pray, and Matthias is chosen

ACT.2.42-42.text: The believers devote themselves to teaching and prayer

ACT.2.43-45.text: The believers share everything with people in need

ACT.2.46-47.text: The believers meet daily, praise God, and grow in number

ACT.3.1-3.text: Peter and John meet a lame beggar at the temple

ACT.3.4-6.text: Peter tells the lame man to walk in Jesus’ name

ACT.3.7-8.text: Peter helps the man up and he walks and praises God

ACT.3.9-10.text: The people recognize the man and are amazed

ACT.3.11-12.text: Peter speaks to the amazed crowd at the temple

ACT.3.13-14.text: Peter says the people rejected Jesus before Pilate

ACT.3.15-16.text: Peter says God raised Jesus and Jesus’ name healed the man

ACT.3.17-18.text: Peter says Christ’s suffering was foretold by the prophets

ACT.3.19-20.text: Peter urges the people to repent and turn back to God

ACT.3.21-23.text: Peter says Moses spoke of a prophet to listen to

ACT.3.24-26.text: Peter says God sent Jesus first to bless the Israelites

ACT.4.5-7.text: The leaders question Peter and John about the healing

ACT.4.11-12.text: Peter says salvation is only in Jesus

ACT.4.26-26.text: The believers quote David about rulers against the Lord

ACT.4.27-28.text: The believers say Herod and Pilate acted against Jesus

ACT.4.29-31.text: The believers ask for boldness and receive the Spirit

ACT.4.32-33.text: The believers share everything with one another

ACT.4.34-35.text: Believers sell property to help those in need

ACT.4.36-37.text: Barnabas gives money from a field he sold

ACT.5.7-8.text: Peter asks Sapphira about the price of the land

ACT.5.14-16.text: More people believe, and the apostles heal the sick

ACT.5.19-21.text: An angel frees the apostles, who go back to teach

ACT.5.26-28.text: The high priest scolds the apostles for teaching

ACT.5.40-42.text: The apostles are flogged and keep teaching about Jesus

ACT.6.2-4.text: The Twelve ask believers to choose seven men to serve

ACT.6.5-6.text: The church chooses seven men, and the apostles pray

ACT.6.7-7.text: The word of God spreads and many priests believe

ACT.6.10-11.text: Stephen’s opponents persuade men to lie about him

ACT.6.12-15.text: Stephen is seized and accused before the Sanhedrin

ACT.7.1-3.text: Stephen tells how God called Abraham to leave his country

ACT.7.4-5.text: God promises the land to Abraham and his descendants

ACT.7.14-14.text: Joseph sends for Jacob and his family

ACT.7.15-16.text: Jacob and the fathers die and are buried in Shechem

ACT.7.31-32.text: The Lord speaks to Moses, and Moses trembles

ACT.7.33-34.text: The Lord sends Moses back to Egypt to free the people

ACT.7.35-37.text: God sends the rejected Moses to rule and save Israel

ACT.7.38-38.text: Moses receives living words at Sinai for the Israelites

ACT.7.39-40.text: The fathers refuse to obey Moses and ask Aaron for gods

ACT.7.41-42.text: The fathers make a calf idol, and God turns away

ACT.7.43-43.text: God says he will send the Israelites into exile

ACT.7.44-46.text: The tabernacle is with the fathers until David’s time

ACT.7.47-50.text: God does not live in houses made by people

ACT.7.51-53.text: Stephen says the leaders always resist the Holy Spirit

ACT.7.54-56.text: Stephen sees Jesus standing at God’s right hand

ACT.7.57-58.text: The crowd drags Stephen out of the city and stones him

ACT.7.59-60.text: Stephen asks Jesus to receive him and forgive his killers

ACT.8.4-5.text: Scattered believers preach, and Philip goes to Samaria

ACT.8.24-24.text: Simon asks the apostles to pray for him

ACT.8.25-25.text: Peter and John preach in Samaria, then return to Jerusalem

ACT.8.32-33.text: The Ethiopian reads about a sheep led to slaughter

ACT.8.34-35.text: Philip tells the Ethiopian the good news about Jesus

ACT.8.36-38.text: Philip baptizes the Ethiopian beside the road

ACT.9.13-16.text: Ananias fears Saul, but the Lord has chosen Saul

ACT.9.26-27.text: Barnabas brings Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem

ACT.9.28-30.text: Saul is sent to Tarsus after Jews try to kill him

ACT.9.40-43.text: Peter raises Tabitha to life, and many in Joppa believe

ACT.10.1-2.text: Cornelius is a devout army officer in Caesarea

ACT.10.3-6.text: An angel tells Cornelius to send men for Peter

ACT.10.19-21.text: The Spirit tells Peter to go with the three men

ACT.10.24-24.text: Peter arrives in Caesarea, where Cornelius waits

ACT.10.25-26.text: Cornelius kneels to worship Peter, but Peter refuses

ACT.10.27-29.text: Peter says God showed him no person is unclean

ACT.10.30-33.text: Cornelius tells of the angel and asks Peter to speak

ACT.10.34-35.text: Peter says God welcomes people from every nation

ACT.10.36-38.text: Peter tells about Jesus, who did good and healed many

ACT.10.39-41.text: Peter says witnesses saw Jesus after God raised him

ACT.10.42-43.text: Peter says everyone who believes in Jesus is forgiven

ACT.10.44-45.text: The Holy Spirit comes on the Gentiles who hear Peter

ACT.10.46-48.text: Peter orders that the Gentiles be baptized

ACT.11.1-3.text: Some believers criticize Peter for eating with Gentiles

ACT.11.4-6.text: Peter tells about his vision of a sheet and animals

ACT.11.7-10.text: Peter tells of the voice that said God made all clean

ACT.11.11-14.text: Peter tells of the three men and the angel’s message

ACT.11.15-16.text: Peter says the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles

ACT.11.17-18.text: The believers praise God for accepting the Gentiles

ACT.11.19-21.text: Believers in Antioch speak to Greeks, and many believe

ACT.11.22-24.text: The church in Jerusalem sends Barnabas to Antioch

ACT.11.25-26.text: Barnabas and Saul teach in Antioch for a year

ACT.11.27-28.text: Agabus predicts a great famine over the whole world

ACT.11.29-30.text: The disciples send gifts to believers in Judea

ACT.12.1-2.text: King Herod kills James and harms the church

ACT.12.3-4.text: Herod arrests Peter and puts him in prison

ACT.12.5-6.text: The church prays for Peter while he sleeps in prison

ACT.12.9-10.text: The angel leads Peter out past the guards and gate

ACT.12.16-17.text: Peter tells the believers how God freed him, then leaves

ACT.12.22-23.text: An angel strikes Herod dead because he took God’s glory

ACT.12.24-25.text: God’s word spreads, and Barnabas and Saul return with John Mark

ACT.13.6-8.text: Elymas the sorcerer opposes Barnabas and Saul at Paphos

ACT.13.11-12.text: Elymas becomes blind and the proconsul believes

ACT.13.13-15.text: Paul and Barnabas go to Antioch and are asked to speak

ACT.13.19-20.text: Paul tells how God gave Israel the land and judges

ACT.13.21-22.text: Paul tells how God gave Israel Saul and then David

ACT.13.23-25.text: Paul says God sent Jesus, and John spoke about him

ACT.13.26-27.text: Paul says the people of Jerusalem did not know Jesus

ACT.13.28-29.text: Paul says Jesus was killed and laid in a tomb

ACT.13.30-31.text: Paul says God raised Jesus and many people saw him

ACT.13.35-37.text: Paul says David’s body decayed but Jesus’s did not

ACT.13.38-39.text: Paul says everyone who believes in Jesus is forgiven

ACT.13.40-41.text: Paul warns the listeners not to reject God’s work

ACT.13.42-43.text: People ask Paul and Barnabas to speak again

ACT.13.44-45.text: Many gather to listen, but some Jews oppose Paul

ACT.13.46-47.text: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles

ACT.13.48-49.text: The Gentiles rejoice and believe, and the word spreads

ACT.14.3-4.text: Paul and Barnabas speak boldly and the city is divided

ACT.14.5-7.text: Paul and Barnabas flee a plot to stone them

ACT.14.8-10.text: Paul heals a man in Lystra who could not walk

ACT.14.11-13.text: The crowds call Barnabas and Paul gods

ACT.14.14-16.text: Paul and Barnabas tell the crowds to turn to the living God

ACT.14.17-18.text: Paul and Barnabas barely stop the crowds from sacrificing

ACT.14.19-20.text: Some Jews stone Paul, but he gets up and goes on

ACT.14.21-22.text: Paul and Barnabas encourage disciples to endure hardship

ACT.14.23-26.text: Paul and Barnabas appoint elders and return to Antioch

ACT.14.27-28.text: Paul and Barnabas tell the church what God did

ACT.15.3-4.text: Paul and Barnabas are welcomed in Jerusalem

ACT.15.5-6.text: Some Pharisee believers say Gentiles must obey the law

ACT.15.19-21.text: James says not to trouble Gentiles who turn to God

ACT.15.33-35.text: Paul and Barnabas stay in Antioch and teach

ACT.15.36-38.text: Paul and Barnabas disagree about taking Mark

ACT.15.39-41.text: Paul and Barnabas part, and Paul takes Silas

ACT.16.4-5.text: The churches grow as Paul delivers the decisions

ACT.16.6-8.text: The Holy Spirit guides Paul’s group to Troas

ACT.16.11-13.text: Paul’s group goes to Philippi and speaks to women

ACT.16.19-21.text: The girl’s owners bring Paul and Silas to the magistrates

ACT.16.22-24.text: Paul and Silas are beaten and put in prison

ACT.16.25-26.text: An earthquake opens the prison while Paul and Silas sing

ACT.16.27-28.text: Paul stops the jailer from killing himself

ACT.16.29-31.text: Paul and Silas tell the jailer to believe in Jesus

ACT.16.32-34.text: The jailer and his household believe and are baptized

ACT.16.35-36.text: The magistrates order Paul and Silas to be released

ACT.16.37-39.text: Paul demands that the magistrates come and escort him out

ACT.16.40-40.text: Paul and Silas encourage believers at Lydia’s house

ACT.17.3-4.text: Paul proves that Jesus is the Christ; some believe

ACT.17.5-7.text: Jealous Jews cause an uproar and accuse Jason

ACT.17.8-9.text: Officials take a bond from Jason and the others

ACT.17.13-15.text: Jews stir up crowds in Berea, so Paul goes to Athens

ACT.17.18-18.text: Philosophers in Athens debate with Paul about Jesus

ACT.17.19-21.text: Athenians ask Paul to explain his new teaching

ACT.17.22-23.text: Paul tells the Athenians about the altar to an unknown god

ACT.17.24-25.text: Paul says God made everything and needs nothing

ACT.17.26-27.text: Paul says God wants all nations to seek him

ACT.17.28-29.text: Paul says God is not like gold, silver or stone images

ACT.17.30-31.text: Paul says God commands all people to repent

ACT.17.32-34.text: Some mock Paul’s message, but others believe

ACT.18.4-6.text: Paul tells the Jews in Corinth he will go to the Gentiles

ACT.18.7-8.text: Paul moves next door, and many Corinthians believe

ACT.18.9-11.text: The Lord tells Paul not to be afraid in Corinth

ACT.18.22-22.text: Paul goes to Caesarea, Jerusalem and Antioch

ACT.18.24-26.text: Priscilla and Aquila teach Apollos in Ephesus

ACT.18.27-28.text: Apollos goes to Achaia and helps believers there

ACT.19.3-4.text: Paul explains John’s baptism to the Ephesian disciples

ACT.19.5-7.text: The disciples are baptized and receive the Holy Spirit

ACT.19.8-10.text: Paul leaves the synagogue and teaches in a lecture hall

ACT.19.11-12.text: God does miracles through Paul to heal the sick

ACT.19.13-14.text: Seven sons of Sceva use the name of Jesus on evil spirits

ACT.19.15-17.text: A man with an evil spirit beats the sons of Sceva

ACT.19.18-20.text: Believers in Ephesus confess and burn magic books

ACT.19.21-22.text: Paul plans to go to Jerusalem and then Rome

ACT.19.26-27.text: Demetrius says Paul is turning people from Artemis

ACT.19.28-29.text: The angry crowd drags Paul’s companions into the theatre

ACT.19.30-32.text: Disciples and officials keep Paul out of the theatre

ACT.19.33-34.text: The Jew Alexander tries to speak, but the crowd shouts

ACT.19.35-37.text: The city clerk tells the crowd to be calm

ACT.19.38-41.text: The city clerk says to settle complaints in court

ACT.20.1-3.text: Paul encourages the believers and goes to Greece

ACT.20.4-6.text: Paul and his companions travel to Troas

ACT.20.7-8.text: Believers meet at Troas and Paul speaks until midnight

ACT.20.9-10.text: Eutychus falls and dies, but Paul says he is alive

ACT.20.11-12.text: Paul speaks until daybreak and Eutychus goes home alive

ACT.20.13-14.text: The ship goes to Assos, where Paul comes aboard

ACT.20.15-16.text: Paul sails past Ephesus to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost

ACT.20.17-21.text: Paul reminds the Ephesian elders how he served

ACT.20.22-24.text: Paul will go to Jerusalem even though danger waits

ACT.20.25-27.text: Paul says the elders will not see him again

ACT.20.28-30.text: Paul warns the elders to guard the church from wolves

ACT.20.31-32.text: Paul puts the elders in God’s care

ACT.20.33-35.text: Paul worked with his hands to help the weak

ACT.20.36-38.text: The elders weep and say goodbye to Paul

ACT.21.1-2.text: Paul and his friends sail on to Patara

ACT.21.3-4.text: Believers in Tyre tell Paul not to go to Jerusalem

ACT.21.5-6.text: The believers in Tyre pray with Paul and say goodbye

ACT.21.7-7.text: Paul and his friends stay one day in Ptolemais

ACT.21.8-9.text: Paul stays with Philip in Caesarea

ACT.21.10-11.text: Agabus says the Jews will bind Paul in Jerusalem

ACT.21.12-14.text: Paul is ready to die in Jerusalem for Jesus

ACT.21.15-16.text: Paul goes to Jerusalem and stays with Mnason

ACT.21.17-19.text: Paul tells James and the elders what God has done

ACT.21.32-33.text: The Roman commander stops the beating and arrests Paul

ACT.21.37-38.text: The commander asks if Paul is a certain Egyptian rebel

ACT.21.39-40.text: Paul tells who he is and speaks to the crowd

ACT.22.9-11.text: Paul is blinded and led into Damascus

ACT.22.12-13.text: Ananias helps Paul to see again

ACT.22.14-16.text: Ananias tells Paul that God has chosen him as a witness

ACT.22.17-18.text: The Lord tells Paul in a vision to leave Jerusalem

ACT.22.25-26.text: Paul tells the centurion he is a Roman citizen

ACT.22.30-30.text: The commander brings Paul before the Sanhedrin

ACT.23.6-8.text: Paul’s words divide the Pharisees and the Sadducees

ACT.23.18-19.text: A centurion takes Paul’s nephew to the commander

ACT.23.20-21.text: Paul’s nephew warns the commander about the ambush

ACT.23.22-22.text: The commander tells the young man to keep it secret

ACT.23.23-24.text: The commander orders soldiers to take Paul to Felix

ACT.24.4-6.text: Tertullus accuses Paul of causing trouble among the Jews

ACT.24.7-9.text: The Jews agree that the charges against Paul are true

ACT.24.10-13.text: Paul says his accusers cannot prove their charges

ACT.24.14-16.text: Paul says he worships God and hopes for a resurrection

ACT.24.17-19.text: Paul says he was clean in the temple and caused no riot

ACT.24.20-21.text: Paul says he is on trial for the resurrection of the dead

ACT.24.22-23.text: Felix delays the decision and lets Paul have some freedom

ACT.24.24-25.text: Paul speaks to Felix and Drusilla, and Felix is afraid

ACT.24.26-27.text: Felix hopes for a bribe and leaves Paul in prison

ACT.25.1-3.text: Jewish leaders ask Festus to bring Paul to Jerusalem

ACT.25.4-5.text: Festus tells the Jewish leaders to accuse Paul in Caesarea

ACT.25.6-8.text: Paul says he has done nothing wrong before Festus

ACT.25.9-9.text: Festus asks Paul if he will go to Jerusalem for trial

ACT.25.10-10.text: Paul says Caesar’s court is the right place for his trial

ACT.25.11-12.text: Paul appeals to Caesar, and Festus agrees to send him

ACT.25.13-16.text: Festus tells King Agrippa about Paul’s case

ACT.25.17-20.text: Festus says the accusers argued about religion and Jesus

ACT.25.21-22.text: Festus says Paul appealed to Caesar; Agrippa wants to listen

ACT.25.23-24.text: Festus presents Paul to Agrippa and the leading men

ACT.25.25-27.text: Festus says Paul did nothing worthy of death

ACT.26.1-3.text: Paul begins his defense before King Agrippa

ACT.26.4-5.text: Paul says the Jews know he lived as a Pharisee

ACT.26.6-8.text: Paul says he is on trial for his hope in God’s promise

ACT.26.9-11.text: Paul tells how he once harmed the believers in Jesus

ACT.26.12-14.text: Paul sees a bright light on the road to Damascus

ACT.26.15-18.text: Jesus appoints Paul to be his servant and witness

ACT.26.19-21.text: Paul obeys the vision and tells all to turn to God

ACT.26.22-23.text: Paul says he teaches what Moses and the prophets said

ACT.26.24-26.text: Festus says Paul is insane, but Paul speaks words of truth

ACT.26.27-29.text: Paul tells Agrippa he wishes all could be like him

ACT.26.30-32.text: Agrippa and Festus agree Paul has done nothing wrong

ACT.27.1-2.text: Paul and other prisoners sail for Italy with Julius

ACT.27.3-6.text: Paul sails past Cyprus and changes ships at Myra

ACT.27.7-8.text: The ship sails slowly to Fair Havens on Crete

ACT.27.9-11.text: Paul warns of danger, but the centurion does not listen

ACT.27.12-12.text: The majority decide to sail on to Phoenix for winter

ACT.27.13-13.text: The sailors leave when a gentle south wind blows

ACT.27.14-16.text: A strong wind called the Northeaster drives the ship

ACT.27.17-18.text: The crew tie the ship with ropes and throw out cargo

ACT.27.19-20.text: The men lose all hope of being saved from the storm

ACT.27.21-22.text: Paul tells the men to be brave; only the ship will be lost

ACT.27.23-26.text: Paul says an angel promised that all on the ship will live

ACT.27.27-29.text: Sailors sense land near and drop four anchors

ACT.27.30-32.text: Paul stops the sailors from escaping in the lifeboat

ACT.27.33-35.text: Paul urges everyone on the ship to eat

ACT.27.36-38.text: The 276 people on the ship eat and throw out the grain

ACT.27.39-41.text: The ship runs aground on a sandbar near a beach

ACT.27.42-44.text: The centurion saves Paul and everyone reaches land safely

ACT.28.1-2.text: The people of Malta are kind and light a fire

ACT.28.3-4.text: A snake bites Paul and islanders think he is guilty

ACT.28.5-6.text: Paul is not hurt, and the islanders say he is a god

ACT.28.7-10.text: Paul heals Publius’s father and other sick people

ACT.28.11-12.text: Paul and the others sail from Malta to Syracuse

ACT.28.13-15.text: Paul reaches Rome, and believers come to meet him

ACT.28.16-18.text: Paul tells the Jewish leaders in Rome why he is a prisoner

ACT.28.19-20.text: Paul says he is bound because of the hope of Israel

ACT.28.21-22.text: The Jewish leaders in Rome want to hear Paul

ACT.28.23-24.text: Paul teaches many people about Jesus; some believe

ACT.28.25-26.text: Paul quotes Isaiah as the Jews disagree and leave

ACT.28.27-27.text: Paul says the people’s hearts have become hard

ACT.28.28-29.text: Paul says God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles

ACT.28.30-31.text: Paul stays two years in Rome and preaches boldly
